source.title: Vessel terms read from the layout of HT 31
source.label: HT 31 layout
source.notes: HT 31 is a list of vessels: its entries pair a word with a vessel ideogram (A402, A410, A415, A416) and a quantity. That the words in it are vessel or container terms follows from the tablet's own layout and is not controversial. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: which pot each word names. The ideogram A402 stands beside three different words on this tablet (lines 2, 9 and 10 of the Unicode text), so a word cannot simply be paired with the sign nearest it, and the tablet is damaged in several places. Proposals identifying particular vessel shapes exist in the literature -- see Y. Duhoux on HT 31 -- and are deliberately not reproduced here, because this file records only what the tablet itself shows. The quantities are worth noting: 10 each of qa-pa3, su-pu and ka-ro-pa3, but 30 sa-ja-ma, 300 su-pa3-ra and 3000 pa-ta-qe, so these are unlikely to all be objects of one kind or size. Check any of this with: python3 -m lineara show 'HT 31'. EXCLUDED: pu-ko and the damaged word ending -ti-sa, which stand in the tablet's opening line rather than in the list body, and so are not shown to be vessel terms.
